chunks: A man from among the scholars was made to sit in his grave, and it was said to him: “Indeed, we shall lash you with one hundred lashes from the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” He said: “I cannot bear it.” They kept pressing him until they reduced it to one. He said: “I cannot bear it.” They said: “There is no escape from it.” He said: “Then for what will you lash me?” They said: “We shall lash you because one day you performed salat without wudu (ablution), and you passed by a weak person and did not help him.” So they lashed him one lash from the punishment of Allah, the Exalted, and his grave was filled with fire.

key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave, the place of post-death reckoning in this report
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for salat

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about praying without wudu (ablution) and failing to help a weak person?
ai.summary: This report describes punishment in the grave for two failures: performing salat without wudu (ablution) and neglecting to aid a weak person. It highlights both ritual responsibility and the duty to support the vulnerable, showing the grave seriousness of these acts in the hereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.130 – (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) ) narrated:

"A certain man from among the scholars was placed in his grave, and it was said to him:
'We will strike you with one hundred lashes from the punishment of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.' He replied: 'I cannot bear it.' They continued to reduce the punishment, until it was brought down to one lash. He said: 'I still cannot bear it.'
They replied: 'It is unavoidable.'
He asked: 'Why will you lash me?'
They said: 'We will lash you because one day you prayed without wudu (ablution), and because you passed by a weak person and did not help him.'
So they lashed him once with a punishment from Allah (swt) the Exalted, and his grave was filled with fire."
